messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV=high — GPU OOM spike on prefill-worker pods in us-west-2 (prefill-pod-08). Trigger: long customer prompt / large context. Paging @oncall_maria :rotating_light:

oncall_maria: I'm on it. Attaching logs now, starting triage.

jonathan_eng: seeing repeated `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` and container restart loop in the last 2m. Logs: 
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:989] failed to allocate 6.43GiB: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
... traceback ...
container "prefill-worker" exited with code 137 (OOM-kill)
```

alice_runtime: this looks like the long-prefill path; prefill path doesn't use kvcache trim fast enough for huge prompts. Can we evict K/V for this tenant and force streaming mode?

devops_sam: I can scale the prefill pool and cordon the failing node to avoid noisy neighbor restarts. Proposing: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/prefill-worker --replicas=18` and `kubectl drain ip-10-0-45-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for the node hosting prefill-pod-08. Any objections?

jonathan_eng: +1 for scaling. Also propose a hotpatch to add an early prefill-size check to reject or fallback for >12000 token prefill requests. We can push a tiny runtime guard and release to canary.

oncall_maria: customer impact: CS reported increased 5xx for one enterprise tenant using very long context ingestion (they sent a 40k token doc). Liz, can you check which accounts affected?

custsuccess_liz: Confirmed: tenant "acme-analytics" saw 71 failed requests in last 10m; SLA alert flagged. I've told them we're investigating and will provide ETA.

alice_runtime: Action items I can do now: enable kvcache aggressive eviction for the tenant (trim to 0.25x), enable `prefill_streaming` fallback for sessions >8k tokens, and release a canary with prefill-size guard. Will push patch to canary in ~7 minutes.

devops_sam: scaling started: `kubectl scale` returned OK, new pods provisioning. Also cordoning node ip-10-0-45-12 and starting drain. If pods fail to reschedule due to binpack, I can provision an emergency GPU node with label `prefill=true`.

oncall_maria: I've applied temporary rate-limit for that tenant: 10 concurrent prefill requests and lowered prefill token cap to 12k for them. This should stop further OOMs while we deploy mitigations.

jonathan_eng: Canary deploy of runtime guard (v1.2.3-hotprefill) rolled to 10% of traffic. Guard rejects >12k with 429 and suggests `use_streaming=true` header. Patch includes a failover to `redwood-medium` model for huge prefill requests.

incident-bot: Update: automatic retries suppressed, circuit-breaker enabled for prefill route.

devops_sam: emergency node up: `gcloud compute instances create gpu-prefill-emer-1 --zone=us-west2-b --labels=prefill=true` and tainted others to prioritize scheduling. New pods coming up.

custsuccess_liz: Customer update draft: "We've identified a spike in GPU OOMs triggered by very large prefill requests from your integration. We've applied temporary rate limits and failover to a smaller model while we deploy a safe guard. Expected full resolution in ~45 minutes. We're monitoring closely." Approve?

oncall_maria: Approve, send now. Include SLA credits note if they request.

alice_runtime: Canary metrics: prefill OOMs dropped to 0 on canary nodes, memory headroom up by ~20%. Rolling to 50% now. I'll also add a regression check to the prefill evals.

jonathan_eng: Root cause hypothesis: no prefill-size validation + large single-tenant burst + K/V cache eviction latency combined with model memory growth for long context. Fix path: short term (rate limit, fallback, kvcache eviction), medium (guard + streaming fallback), long term (memory compaction, smarter kv eviction and per-tenant soft quotas).

devops_sam: All actions executed: node drained, scaled to 18, emergency node online, canary release in progress. Will keep ops-bridge open for 1h.

ops-bridge: Bridge started by oncall_maria. Link: https://meet.company/bridge/2765432100

oncall_maria: Handoff for night shift: monitor OOM rate on prefill-worker (metric: inference.prefill.oom.count) and ensure canary rollout completes to 100% before removing rate limits. If OOMs recur, revert canary and escalate to eng-runtime pager.

custsuccess_liz: Update sent to customer. They acknowledged and asked for postmortem and param change suggestions for their ingestion script.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: SEV=high — mitigation in place (rate limits + fallback + canary). Keep channel updated with any regressions.

oncall_maria: Closing handoff — monitoring only. Thanks team :heart:
